readerContract.humanQuestion: What is CRISP doing with frozen tissue slides during an operation, what did this study test, and what remains unproved?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Explain the urgent frozen-section job, the comparison result and why observed model performance is not proof of better care.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No pathology, statistics or computer-vision knowledge is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A frozen section gives a pathologist a quick intraoperative tissue image. CRISP compares patterns in that image with learned patterns; the paper tests that support, not patient outcomes.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A reader sees a medical-AI headline and needs to know whether it reports a research result, a clinical trial or proven improvement in care.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A concise September 12 research explanation of the September 10 accepted Nature Medicine article.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can explain what the model did and why this study is not proof of better care.

canonicalTruth.owner: The Nature Medicine accepted paper owns the study design, methods, results and limitations; the journal landing page owns the September 10 publication metadata.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Reopen the journal record and current paper version before publication or after a correction or Version of Record replaces the preview.

strengthsToUse: Make one distinction do useful work across the article
Keep an evidence limit next to the claim it limits

candidateRepairPreflight.studyVersion: Current accepted manuscript governs: 103,797 slides obtained primarily from ten centres; no older eight-centre scope is imported.
candidateRepairPreflight.studyDesign: Prospective observational, not interventional; retrospectively registered.
candidateRepairPreflight.simulation: The 100-case deployment and timing analysis is explicitly simulated.
candidateRepairPreflight.nonClaims: No clinical impact, patient benefit, local availability, regulation, treatment recommendation or medical advice.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: CRISP was tested on fast frozen-section images during surgery and outperformed the other models compared in the study; it has not yet been shown to improve patient outcomes.
causalSequence: A frozen section is prepared quickly while surgery continues.
CRISP analyses that image and offers a prediction for a pathologist to interpret.
The study compares model predictions under stated observational conditions.
A later interventional study would be needed to show whether care or outcomes improve.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: The paper compares CRISP with other foundation models across the evaluated tasks and separately reports a senior pathologist as comparable overall in the reader study.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: For another medical-AI paper, ask whether the evidence measured a model score, professional workflow, treatment decision or patient outcome.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: When reading medical-AI news, separate comparison performance from evidence that care or outcomes improved.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Lead with the frozen-section job and study design; omit promotional percentages, medical advice and implied availability.

discoveryChecks.question: Did the study test better patient outcomes?
discoveryChecks.answer: No; the authors say an interventional study is still needed.

discoveryChecks.question: Was the 100-case deployment observed routine care?
discoveryChecks.answer: No; the paper calls it simulated deployment.

discoveryChecks.question: Is CRISP presented as available locally?

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Observational or simulated findings could be rewritten as proof of clinical benefit.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Require exact study-design and limitations excerpts, full source accounting and an explicit no-outcome sentence before root review.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can distinguish model/workflow evaluation from an interventional patient-outcome study.
